newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian premier's business links under fire.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian premier's business links under fire.

text.p: The deputy head of Bulgaria's parliamentary commission against corruption asked the chief prosecutor on Thursday to investigate Prime Minister Zhan Videnov's business links.

Edvin Sugarev, a member of parliament from the opposition Union of Democratic Forces, said Videnov and senior officials had permitted the establishment of a group of companies known as the Orion Group and done nothing to curb its activities.
"Orion has caused significant losses to different state and private financial institutions," he said in a letter to chief prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev, a copy of which was sent to Reuters.
Sugarev asked Tatarchev to investigate Videnov and six senior officials for possible corruption, misuse of public funds and abuse of power.

"Zhan Videnov has full information on the illegal activity of Orion and its bank, the Bulgarian Agricultural and Industrial Bank, and despite this he has done nothing to prevent the damage they cause the state, private individuals and agricultural corporations," he said.
Sofia City Court cancelled the bank's registration this year, citing legal inconsistencies in the list of shareholders, and appointed liquidators to close it down.
A home-made car bomb damaged the chief liquidator's car on October 31 but no one was hurt.
Orion was at the centre of a political row last year after Bulgaria exported large quantities of grain at high world prices, creating shortages at home.

Videnov has denied in parliament that companies known as the Orion group because they bear the names of stars in the Orion constellation had any formal links. He says they are only "a friendly circle."
Sugarev's letter to Tatarchev also said there were irregularities at the state refinery Neftohim and the State Savings Bank.
He condemned central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov for allowing the refinancing of collapsing state and private commercial banks, which he said had caused losses worth 10 billion levs.

A quarter of Bulgaria's numerous and illiquid banks are now in receivership. Loss of confidence in the banking system caused a run on the lev, which has fallen from 70 to the dollar at the beginning of the year to about 500 now.
Videnov is under pressure both from the opposition and from reformists in his Socialist party over his handling of the economic crisis.
A party congress this weekend will discuss reformists' calls for a new cabinet and for separation of the functions of party chairman and prime minister.
